About me

I’m a data analyst with a Master of Technology in Computer Science and Engineering. I like turning large, messy datasets into clear visuals that help people make decisions. My work covers sales, payroll, HR, finance and project performance.

My process is simple: clean and transform data in Power Query, model it with DAX measures, and present KPIs, trends and variances so stakeholders can decide quickly. I care most about reports that are accurate, easy to read and end in a clear recommendation.

I’m now looking for a data analyst role where I can keep turning data into clear decisions.

Project 01 · Power BI

Sales Overview Dashboard

Goal

Show where sales come from and where the business should grow.

What I built

KPI cards, monthly trend, zone, customer-type and product-type breakdowns, a year funnel, a market map and slicers for month, year, zone and customer type.

Key insights

  • April was the peak month: 4.74M total sales at an 11.4% profit margin.
  • North zone led with about 3.56M; South contributed about 0.51M.
  • Brick and mortar made up 85.77% of sales; e-commerce 14.23%.
  • Delhi NCR was the strongest market. Recommended: expand in weaker regions and grow e-commerce.
Sales OverviewClick image to zoom
Project 02 · Power BI

Payroll Analysis Dashboard

Goal

Give finance and HR one place to track payroll cost, overtime and department spend.

What I built

A 4-page report for 130 employees (Aug 2026): overview, department payroll statement, account summary and employee details, with a department filter.

Key insights

  • Gross payroll 168.86K and net payroll 154.19K, up 2.71K on the previous month.
  • IT had the highest gross payroll (39.52K) and the most overtime.
  • Operations had the highest average cost per employee (1,553).
  • Total overtime was 994 hours, costing 4.20K.
OverviewClick image to zoom
Project 03 · Tableau

HR Recruitment Dashboard

Goal

Understand which sources and departments produce hires, and where hiring slows down.

What I built

KPI tiles, recruitment funnel, source share and source analysis, department hiring, duration by department, and filters for stage, role, department and source.

Key insights

  • 319 candidates led to 27 hires: an 8.46% hire rate and 11.8 candidates per hire.
  • The company website was the best source: 11.94% hire rate and 8 hires.
  • IT had the most hires (10) and the longest time to final stage.

Project 04 · Excel

Employee Attendance Dashboard

Goal

Spot attendance problems early and flag employees who need follow-up.

What I built

KPI cards, editable targets (95% attendance, flag below 92%, flag at 10+ late days), a risk-tier score, leave bands and a top 10 late arrivals list for Jan to Aug 2026.

Key insights

  • Attendance was 95.2% overall, above the 95% target, with a 4.0% late rate.
  • Leave days peaked in August (151); attendance was highest in July (95.8%).
  • 23 policy flags raised; 16 employees in the high-risk tier.
  • 13 employees (10%) took 13 or more leave days.

Project 05 · Power BI

Project Performance Dashboard

Goal

Give stakeholders real-time visibility of project progress, finances and risks.

What I built

KPI cards, a project pipeline funnel, a risk donut chart, a project category chart and three switchable views (Financial Progress, Physical Progress, Progress Difference) driven by DAX measures and slicers.

Key insights

  • Tracked 1,836 projects through 6 pipeline stages, from DPR Approved (1,797) to Completed (367).
  • Monitored ₹3,487 Cr in awarded value, with 24.80% financial progress and 89.57% bill clearance.
  • Natural causes were the largest risk share (41.67% of 36 risks).
